                    ### Question
                    A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents for a routine colonoscopy. A polyp is found in the patient's transverse colon and is found to be cancerous on histological evaluation. Upon examination, it is found that these cancerous cells have decreased MHC class I expression on their surface. Which immune system cell is most capable of killing these tumor cells?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Natural killer cells
opb. B-cells
opc. Macrophages
opd. Eosinophils
ope. Cytotoxic T-cells

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the context of decreased MHC class I expression on tumor cells, the immune system cell most capable of killing these cells is the natural killer (NK) cell. Standard medical consensus indicates that cytotoxic T-cells require MHC class I molecules to recognize and kill target cells. When MHC class I expression is reduced, cytotoxic T-cell activity is impaired. However, NK cells are specifically activated by the absence or low expression of MHC class I molecules, as they recognize this as a sign of abnormality or stress in cells. The retrieved evidence paths, while broad, support the interaction between NK cells and tumor cells, aligning with the consensus that NK cells can effectively target and kill tumor cells with decreased MHC class I expression. Therefore, the correct answer is that natural killer cells are most capable of killing these tumor cells.
